speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had a chronic cough with recurrent bronchitis; have you noticed any hemoptysis, weight loss, or night sweats? REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture_AND_Sensitivity. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news; normal sputum and CT findings help rule out tuberculosis and lung cancer. To further investigate the cause of your recurrent infections, do you currently smoke or have a history of significant environmental exposure to dust or chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very specific description; does the "thick, foamy, yellow-green" sputum ever contain visible blood or rust-colored flecks, and have you noticed any swelling in your fingers or toes? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay_Posterior_Anterior.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Excellent, the normal gas exchange and chest X-ray further rule out severe pneumonia or interstitial lung disease. Given your long history of recurrent infections and the specific color of your sputum, have you noticed any clubbing of your fingers, and do you have a history of sinus problems or dental issues?

REQUEST TEST: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin_Level.
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. While Alpha-1 Antitrypsin deficiency is a differential, the normal levels combined with your long-standing history of copious purulent sputum and recurrent infections strongly point to bronchiectasis. Would you be willing to undergo a high-resolution CT scan to visualize the dilated bronchi and confirm this diagnosis?
